A_target.statement:
Let $G = \struct {L, R, E}$ be a finite [[Definition:Bipartite Graph|bipartite graph]].
Then the maximum size of a [[Definition:Matching (Graph Theory)|matching]] equals the minimum size of a [[Definition:Vertex Cover|vertex cover]].

B_source.statement: In a [[Definition:Flow Network|flow network]] with integer capacities, the maximum value of an $s$-$t$ flow equals the minimum capacity of an $s$-$t$ cut, and an integral maximum flow exists.

substitutions.the network: s -> u of capacity 1 for u in L, u -> v of infinite capacity for edges, v -> t of capacity 1 for v in R

object_map.reformulation: Build the matching network with infinite middle capacities, so that finite cuts are exactly vertex covers.

validity_conditions: Infinite capacity on the middle arcs forces every finite cut to cut only source and sink arcs.
Integrality of the maximum flow is needed to read off a matching.
proof_plan: Build the network with arcs $s \to u$ of capacity $1$ for $u \in L$, $u \to v$ of capacity $\infty$ for $u v \in E$, and $v \to t$ of capacity $1$ for $v \in R$.
An integral flow sends one unit along disjoint paths $s \to u \to v \to t$, so the maximum flow value is the maximum matching size.

Let $\tuple {S, T}$ be a finite cut with $s \in S$.
No arc $u \to v$ goes from $S$ to $T$, so the cut arcs are $s \to u$ for $u \in L \cap T$ and $v \to t$ for $v \in R \cap S$.
Then $C = \paren {L \cap T} \cup \paren {R \cap S}$ is a vertex cover with $\card C$ equal to the capacity, and every vertex cover arises this way.
